sources.citation: Palfreyman, Nicholas. 2015. Sign language varieties of Indonesia: A linguistic and sociolinguistic investigation. PhD thesis, University of Central Lancashire.
sources.note: Nothing language-specific. Corpus is from Solo and Makassar, not Yogyakarta; p.19 surveys prior Yogyakarta work (Bharoto 2013 classifiers, Sukmara 2014 'phonological components', Isma 2012, Suwiryo 2013 mouthings, Woodward & Bharoto 2011 dictionary). 'Stress' appears only generically in ch.3 as one of the 'phonological and prosodic considerations such as rhythm, stress and intonation (Crasborn, 2006; Sandler, 2012)' affecting sign articulation in connected signing, and in the Haspelmath clitic criterion ('prototypical clitics do not bear their own stress'). No statement about prominence place…
